comparator.name: Law (Rechtsgeleerdheid)
comparator.sourceNotes: Tilburg’s current official 2026–27 curriculum accounts for exactly 180 ECTS. Year 1 contains ten compulsory 6-ECTS courses (60 ECTS), year 2 contains ten compulsory 6-ECTS courses (60 ECTS), and year 3 contains 42 ECTS of compulsory law, society, moot-court, comparative-law, labour-law, civil-procedure and thesis work plus an 18-ECTS minor or mobility window. Zero-credit Dutch-language testing, mentoring and the Tilburg Skills Lab are retained as programme features but excluded from the credit total. The page also lists a 30-ECTS exchange option without specifying which 12 compulsory ECTS it replaces; this decision therefore preserves the internally complete 42+18 standard minor structure and does not invent an exchange substitution.

components.name: Mobility Window / minor
components.note: Genuine 18-ECTS open minor or mobility space. Tilburg names Law in Practice and Law and a Sustainable Future among the substantive options; no single option is imposed on the comparator reconstruction.

progressionAssessment.rationale: Law, Society & Justice in semester 1 precedes every advanced law course that formally requires it. Research Methods & Statistics precedes the selected economics courses with that prerequisite. Every course is offered in its assigned term and every formal prerequisite is completed in an earlier semester.

notes.text: Tilburg’s Rechtsgeleerdheid is a Dutch-law degree with a continuous doctrinal sequence, procedural-law practice, a zero-credit Skills Lab, an integrated moot court and an 8-ECTS legal thesis. UCR can assemble a substantial interdisciplinary law pathway across private, criminal, constitutional, EU, international and human-rights law, but it does not reproduce the full Dutch professional-law curriculum or its integrated practice sequence.

UCR has no dedicated equivalents for Tilburg’s Dutch administrative-law procedure, tax law, property and contract sequence, liability law, labour law, civil procedure, legal-history sequence or integrated Skills Lab and moot-court training. Adjacent politics, business, communication, sustainability and technology courses broaden the UCR alternatives without being treated as direct replacements for those specialist components.

The Tilburg programme is Dutch-taught and includes a compulsory zero-credit Dutch-language test; UCR is English-taught. The comparison assesses academic content and structure rather than language eligibility.
